correctness.rationale: The three-circle intersection gives exact line-coordinate intervals. The diameter bound confines relevant offsets to O(sqrt(epsilon)); angular end strips contribute O(epsilon). Away from strips the controlling disk endpoints yield an exact differentiable root with q_e(alpha)=epsilon cot(alpha)+O(epsilon^2 cot^3(alpha)). The error integrates to O(epsilon), while 2epsilon integral cot gives exactly epsilon log(1/epsilon) per angle sector. Threefold symmetry and constant unit width normalize the coefficient to 3/pi. Standalone numerical quadrature corroborates the leading term.

value.rationale: The geometric observable is the natural long-chord probability of a classical constant-width body. The sharp epsilon log(1/epsilon) law with explicit 3/pi coefficient exposes how arc–vertex competition changes endpoint scaling relative to a circle, and may inform inverse geometric-probability and nonsmooth approximation work. The claim does not rest on an arbitrary isolated numerical parameter.
